name: Covariance
description:
Covariance allows a child's method to return a more specific type than the return type of its parent's method.

This means that the type of the return value in the method ``trumpet`` of the child class ``Calf`` can be a child of the type of the return value in the method ``trumpet`` of the parent class ``AfricanElephpant``.

Less specific types can be: the same type ``AfricanElephpant``, a child class of the ``AfricanElephpant`` type, here ``Calf``, an intersection type, such as ``AfricanElephpant&Z``. In particular, the type may not become nullable.

It cannot be a totally different type, a union type, such as ``AfricanElephpant|A``, any class that implements the same interfaces as ``AfricanElephpant``, or a different scalar type.
code:
<?php

    class Elephpant {}

    class AfricanElephpant extends Elephpant {
        function trumpet() : AfricanElephpant { }
    }

    class Calf extends AfricanElephpant {
        // This method returns an object compatible with AfricanElephpant, but more specific
        function trumpet() : Calf { }
    }

?>
